messages.content: 在壓力為10千帕的情況下，水的凝固點是多少？

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit of the pressure. Default is 'kPa'.

message.content:
**Answer**

At a pressure of **10 kPa**, the freezing point of pure water rises to roughly **+6.7 °C**.  
This shift is due to the fact that ice occupies a larger volume than liquid water; when the external pressure is lowered, the system compensates by freezing at a higher temperature.

---

### Why the tool isn’t used here

The available function `thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point` only computes boiling points, not freezing points. Since you asked for the freezing point, I calculated it directly using the Clausius–Clapeyron relation for the ice–water transition:

\[
\frac{dT}{dP} \approx \frac{T\,\Delta V}{\Delta H}
\]

With \( \Delta V \approx -9\times10^{-5}\,\text{m}^3/\text{kg} \) (difference between liquid and solid densities) and \( \Delta H \approx 333.5\,\text{kJ}/\text{kg} \), the slope is about \(-7.4\times10^{-5}\,\text{K/Pa}\).  
Applying this to the pressure drop from 101.3 kPa to 10 kPa gives an increase of about 6.7 K, so the freezing point becomes ~6.7 °C.

If you need the boiling point at 10 kPa instead, let me know and I’ll call the function for you.
